title: Jev moves from typed judgments to practical application patterns
summary: Conference examples and current cookbooks show how to compose Jev into routing, retrieval and presentation tools, with corrected aliases and explicit limits on confidence and automation.

sections.title: What the November examples add
sections.html:
Jev is most useful when software needs a semantic judgment and already has a defined action to take afterward. A teacher’s resource finder can rank relevant lessons; a help screen can suggest a destination; a presenter’s checklist can recognize a point expressed in different words. The application can keep its ordinary controls, state and permission rules while using the model for the part that depends on meaning. My assessment remains positive for a bounded pilot with an inspectable output and a clear fallback.

The new evidence is practical rather than a new model release. Richard MacManus’s November 12 conference report describes Glean using Jev alongside other model types, UiPath experimenting with tournament-style document ranking, and Workday prototyping a form that begins filling while someone types. These are reported uses and demonstrations, not independently reproduced deployments. The demonstrations’ speed claims do not establish latency for a different application. Conference reporting.

Official material now makes several patterns concrete: ask independent questions together, combine scores in code, rerank an existing shortlist, and maintain a checklist from transcript judgments. This revision develops those workflows and corrects the earlier alias snapshot. Jev 1.14 still dates to October 14; the November coverage should not be presented as another model launch. The release’s experimental image, Box and extended-context features remain a separate adoption decision from the text workflow. Model changelog.

sections.title: State, parallel questions and software-owned policy
sections.html:
The API accepts state and named, typed questions. Choice selects an option; Score evaluates ordered levels; Noul estimates the probability of a yes answer. Answers retain their question names, and the response includes model and token-usage information. A well-formed answer can still misunderstand the supplied evidence. Typed output makes a result easier to consume, while product logic must decide what it means for a user. System One API.

TypeSafe’s speculative fan-out pattern puts possible branch questions in the same request. Its support example asks for a category alongside details relevant only to bugs or billing. Code reads the applicable answers after classification and ignores the others. This avoids a dependent follow-up when all necessary evidence was already available. It does not make questions dependent on each other: a question cannot use an answer that has not yet been returned. Speculative fan-out.

A proposed teaching-site version would ask whether a request concerns navigation, a lesson explanation or a broken exercise. It could also ask which lesson section is relevant and whether an error description contains reproducible steps. The application would use only the selected branch, show the suggested route, and retain a manual choice. Independent answers should not quietly authorize account changes or overwrite work.

For ranking, the composite-scoring pattern separates dimensions and combines them with explicit weights. That lets an editor change priorities without rerunning unchanged judgments. Composite scoring. In a lesson library, relevance and language complexity might be compensating preferences, while unavailable equipment should be a separate exclusion rule. A weighted average must not erase a condition the product treats as mandatory.

sections.title: Probability, confidence and correctness need separate treatment
sections.html:
TypeSafe’s confidence reference now makes an especially useful distinction: confidence summarizes the concentration of an answer distribution. For Choice, it derives from the leading probability and number of options; for Score, it also accounts for distance between ordered levels. Noul returns its yes probability without a separate confidence field. The same displayed confidence can therefore correspond to different top probabilities across different Choice sizes. It is not an independent measurement of real-world correctness. Confidence definitions.

The documentation recommends considering the probability of the particular action-relevant option, and tuning thresholds on the intended workload. For a fixed Choice size, checking both top probability and its confidence transformation does not add independent evidence. A Score average can also conceal probability split between distant levels. These distinctions matter when an interface turns a numerical answer into a label such as complete, relevant or safe.

A practical evaluation should keep the distribution, question definition, model version, input revision and resulting action. Review confident errors as well as uncertain cases. If two routes repeatedly compete, improve their definitions or add a clarification path. If no option fits, provide an explicit no-match outcome instead of forcing an apparently confident choice. These are proposed product safeguards, not guarantees supplied by the model.

Thresholds should reflect what a mistaken suggestion costs. Opening a reversible help panel can tolerate different errors from changing a learner’s plan. For the latter, start with teacher review and compare the suggestions against an agreed evaluation set. Neither a sharp distribution nor the vendor’s calibration language establishes calibration on classroom material, accessibility requests or a particular language.

sections.title: A rehearsal checklist with an inspectable failure mode
sections.html:
TypeSafe’s Intelliprompter cookbook is a more concrete starting point than a generic lesson-planner proposal. The documented application accumulates a transcript, scores each unchecked talking point, and stores completion in ordinary code. Its published replay uses six transcript chunks and identifies Jev 1.14 with a November 4 run date. The cookbook describes a microphone and ElevenLabs integration but omits that integration code; it demonstrates the TypeSafe portion. Intelliprompter cookbook.

The example’s 2.5 threshold on a displayed one-to-five coverage scale is a local completion rule, not a Jev confidence value. Once a criterion is checked, it stays checked and leaves subsequent requests. Jev supplies scores; the application owns the persistent state. That distinction makes the interface predictable, but also creates a visible failure mode: a premature check will not automatically correct itself later.

For a teacher rehearsing a short explanation, the input could be a teacher-authored outline and a consented transcript. Ask whether the explanation states the learning objective, gives the planned example and includes a check for understanding. The output should be an editable checklist next to the actual transcript, with a way to reopen an incorrectly completed item. Keep this separate from grading students or claiming that the lesson produced learning.

The integration still needs a transcription provider, a server-side TypeSafe call, state storage, request coordination and a usable review screen. A small acceptance set should include paraphrases, negations, a point mentioned only as something to avoid, transcription errors and unfinished examples. Compare checklist changes with a teacher’s labels. Measure premature checks, missed coverage and correction effort; a high overall match rate can conceal the one false completion that changes how someone prepares.

Start with recorded rehearsal text before live audio. This isolates the judgment loop from transcription and network failures. Only add live updates after the checklist behavior is useful, and make the displayed transcript revision clear so a late response cannot be mistaken for an assessment of newer speech.

sections.title: Retrieval, websites and video production
sections.html:
A website can use Jev after a conventional search system has retrieved candidates. The official reranking cookbook applies a Noul question to each query–passage pair and sorts the results. Its example uses a BM25 shortlist of 30 passages for 40 CLERC queries. This is a specific vendor demonstration, not evidence that the same accuracy improvement transfers to lessons, product documentation or film transcripts. A reranker cannot recover a useful passage that the first stage omitted. Reranking cookbook.

A proposed educational resource browser would retrieve a small set of attributable passages, judge their relevance to the teacher’s query, and show the ranked source links with snippets. Its acceptance test should separate retrieval recall from reranking order. Include queries with no answer and similar-looking passages that discuss a topic without answering the question. Keep the original ranking available during the pilot so editors can see which changes helped.

For a creative app, a transcript review queue is a suitable extension. Supply one segment with the production outline and ask separate questions about topic coverage, repetition and whether a visual explanation would help. Return segment identifiers and judgments to the editor, who can inspect the source and choose cuts. This is an editorial proposal; it does not establish automatic fact-checking, good pacing or support for any particular editing application.

For a video presenter, the documented checklist pattern can mark planned points during rehearsal or flag omissions before recording another take. Jev does not natively accept audio or video according to the current model reference. Transcription, timestamps, media decoding and timeline integration remain external responsibilities. Experimental still-image questions can be explored separately, but a correctly shaped bounding box does not prove it located the intended object. Keep any frame experiment out of the text pilot’s success claim.

sections.title: Current access and a versioned operating plan
sections.html:
As checked on November 14, the model reference maps both jev-latest and jev-preview to jev-1.14.0, with no separate preview build currently listed. This corrects the October snapshot in which the aliases differed. The listed price remains $0.042 per million input tokens, with free output, and default limits of 64k tokens per request and 32k per question. Both limits increase to 262k with the long-context header; the documentation warns of speed and accuracy tradeoffs. These are service terms at retrieval, not measured charges. Current models and limits.

Pin a version while evaluating and record the returned model identifier. Replay representative cases before moving to another version or a moving alias. An unchanged application can otherwise acquire different routing behavior. Track the fraction of requests requiring review as well as correctness: a change that maintains accuracy by escalating almost everything may remove the feature’s practical value.

Access requires an authenticated hosted API request. Rate limits depend on the organization, and the public documentation does not establish this user’s allowance or service availability. No account was opened and no API call was made for this report. A low token price should be evaluated alongside retries, transcription, engineering and human review; this research measured none of those costs.

TypeSafe’s legal index states a commitment not to train on customer data and points to the governing agreements. It describes zero data retention as an enterprise offering, rather than a default entitlement for every user. Legal and data-handling index. Before sending school or production material, check the applicable account terms and use only the data the task needs. The inspected sources establish hosted access, not downloadable model weights or local inference.

sections.title: What should earn a place in the product
sections.html:
The strongest reason to try Jev is the application structure it supports: narrow semantic judgments, reusable probabilities and explicit code that turns them into behavior. The strongest reason to keep the pilot bounded is that neither type safety nor decomposition proves the final workflow correct. A useful question can be answered wrongly, and several plausible answers can combine into an unhelpful action.

Choose one output that a person can inspect: a suggested help route, a ranked source list or a rehearsal checklist. Define the acceptance set and failure path before connecting it to live users. Keep the original input visible, allow correction, and review whether the tool saves work after errors are included. Avoid turning a useful rehearsal aid into a claim about learner outcomes, or a conference prototype into a promise of production performance.

This update combines reported conference examples with primary API, pattern and cookbook documentation. It does not reproduce the conference demonstrations, run a model comparison, listen to generated audio or measure classroom gains. The worker used public web extracts because its browser surface was unavailable. The detailed model-jaggedness page also remained inaccessible after one repair; no new language-specific performance conclusion is drawn from it.

A successful experiment should earn a specific function. Stop or narrow it if users cannot understand a result, corrections do not persist, or review effort exceeds the benefit. The November material gives builders better starting designs and more precise operational distinctions. Whether those designs are reliable enough for a particular product remains an empirical question for that product.

useCases: Suggest help routes with explicit fallback
Rerank an attributable lesson or documentation library
Review rehearsal coverage from an external transcript
Queue transcript segments for an editor
limitations: Conference deployments and demonstrations are reported, not independently reproduced.
No authenticated API call, latency/cost measurement or classroom trial.
Images, Box and extended context remain separately gated experimental features.
Hosted access does not establish open weights or local portability.
Confidence summarizes distributions; task-specific evaluation and application-owned policy remain necessary.
Worker browser unavailable; public web extracts used. Model-jaggedness page inaccessible after one repair.

judgment: Worth a bounded pilot in routing, retrieval or rehearsal review, with explicit criteria, a pinned version, visible source material and a measured correction path.
researchNote: Original report and October14 model-release chronology retained. Material November14 revision incorporates November12 conference reporting, current official patterns and a November4 Intelliprompter replay; corrects aliases without implying a new model launch. Worker used web.run public extracts after IAB availability failures; no Chrome claim for this acquisition, no API or media test. Application workflows and acceptance criteria are editorial proposals.
